set.descent_text: The route ends on the flat ground of the Upper Saddle, about 100 to 200 ft up and left of the top of the Black Ice Couloir, just under the boulder problem that leads to the Owen-Spalding rappels. From there continue to the summit of the Grand Teton, or descend: do not drop into the first gully heading southeast; go farther west to the climbers trails that lead down to the Lower Saddle, then follow Garnet Canyon out.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Cross it below the Enclosure Ice Couloir and past the Emotional Rescue Buttress, gain the Black Ice Couloir by a single rock or mixed pitch, and follow it for several hundred feet to the bowl below the West Face. There, angle left to a pinned anchor under the steeper ground's left fork. That fork is Alberich's Alley; the right fork is the Black Ice itself.

review.notes: Alberich page for traverse, fork and Upper Saddle finish; Black Ice page for the entry pitch; Grand Teton batch sources for the saddle descent.

set.descent_text: The couloir ends at the Upper Saddle. From there use any of several routes to the summit, or descend by the Owen-Spalding line. Do not drop into the first gully heading southeast from the saddle; go farther west to the climbers trails that lead down to the Lower Saddle, then follow Garnet Canyon out. Parties on the Owen-Spalding above can send rockfall onto the upper couloir.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. A cairn standing out on the Southwest Ridge skyline, seen from the Lower Saddle, marks where the traverse goes; getting there means crossing several gullies and small ribs, which is awkward. Beyond it, easy ledges lead around the northwest corner of the ridge, after which the ground becomes serious. Rotten ledges lead onward until the whole peak is in view; head for the foot of the large icefield under the upper West Face. A last short headwall of awkward 5.6 to 5.7 rock leads to the ice.

review.notes: Route page for traverse, cairn, rockfall and Upper Saddle finish; Grand Teton batch for the saddle descent.

set.descent_text: The final stretch is roughly 400 to 600 ft of easy fifth-class and fourth-class ridge toward the top of the Vision Quest Couloir, which ends on the Enclosure summit. Descend as for the standard Enclosure line: pick your way down the easy ground toward the Upper Saddle, then follow the climbers trail to the Lower Saddle.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Complete it to the Enclosure Ice Couloir, where the route's crack system is plainly in view. A lower ramp system leads to an upper ramp beneath the first pitch; snow and ice may lie across the base of the buttress.

review.notes: Route page for approach and top-out; Vision Quest and Lookin for Trouble pages cross-check the ridge ending at the Enclosure summit.

set.descent_text: The couloir ends at the notch in the Northwest Ridge. From there either continue up the ridge to the summit of the Enclosure and descend the standard way, or descend the far side by rappel to get back onto the Valhalla Traverse, which leads to the Lower Saddle.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Going around behind the Enclosure, the first couloir on your right is the Enclosure Ice Couloir. Farther along, up and to the left, the traverse arrives at the Black Ice Couloir. The couloir is about 50 degrees and the route finding is easy.

review.notes: Route page for couloir, notch and rappel option; Black Ice page for the traverse.

set.descent_text: The route finishes with easy fifth-class climbing and scrambling to the summit of the Enclosure. Descend toward the Upper Saddle by the easy ground, then follow the climbers trail down to the Lower Saddle and out Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. The approach is the same as for the Enclosure Ice Couloir: go around the back of the Enclosure to the base of that couloir. From there, easy but rotten ice and broken rock lead to the start of the obvious chimney and wide crack system.

review.notes: Route page and the AAJ note agree on the Lower Saddle and Valhalla Traverse approach and the summit finish.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Follow it as for the Black Ice Couloir to the foot of the Black Ice entry. The line is the prominent right-facing corner and ramp system directly below the Vision Quest Couloir.

review.notes: Route page places the start; descent left out because no page says where the route tops out.

set.descent_text: The couloir ends only about 100 ft below the Enclosure summit, and finishes on the Enclosure; from there you can continue to the Grand Teton or descend. Go down the easy ground toward the Upper Saddle, then follow the climbers trail to the Lower Saddle and out Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Follow it to the Black Ice Couloir and climb its entry pitch, then the Black Ice's snow and ice to a point where a narrower couloir splits off to the right, facing the foot of the Great West Chimney. A short section of mixed climbing at its start leads to the ice.

review.notes: Route page and the AAJ note agree the route leaves the Black Ice and ends on the Enclosure summit; distance up the Black Ice differs between them, so none is given.

set.descent_text: The route arrives at the top of the Enclosure after crossing the Vision Quest Couloir high on the face. The standard descent from there is the easy ground toward the Upper Saddle and then the couloir and climbers trail down to the Lower Saddle.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Follow it to the Enclosure Ice Couloir, climb a short way up the couloir, then step left into the corner system, which lies on the right-hand side of the Enclosure's big rock feature.

review.notes: Route page for approach and top-out; descent follows the Enclosure summit descent from the South Coulior and Jim's Big Day pages.

set.descent_text: A knife-edge and then an exposed fourth-class ridge scramble finish on the Enclosure summit. The usual climbers trail takes you back down to the Lower Saddle.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The route is clearly visible from the Lower Saddle. Hike a short way up the standard approach toward the Upper Saddle, watching for a high rock pillar to the left of, and above, the Eye of the Needle. At that point cross the Idaho Express Couloir to an obvious ledge system near the start, traverse over the couloir, and stop for the belay on its far side where falling rock cannot reach.

review.notes: Route page for approach, ending and descent; South Coulior page for the Enclosure summit descent.

set.descent_text: The route joins Emotional Rescue at its eighth pitch, then 400 to 600 ft of easy fifth- and fourth-class terrain leads to the top of the Enclosure. Descend toward the Upper Saddle by the easy ground, then follow the climbers trail down to the Lower Saddle and out Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Follow it to the foot of the Black Ice Couloir. The first moves are around 30 ft above the start of the Black Ice's opening rock pitch, in a left-facing corner with a black band.

review.notes: Route page for start and finish; Emotional Rescue page for the shared top section.

wy_northwest_ridge_3.skip_reason: route page only gives the upper third from the Valhalla Traverse ledge; no text on the lower approach or where it tops out, so no descent or approach can be written

set.descent_text: Reverse the route: the easy ground east of the summit leads toward the Upper Saddle, then the climbers trail drops through the gully beside the Needle to the Lower Saddle. If you followed the couloir in early season, snow can be steep and exposed rock loose, so an axe and crampons are prudent on the way down. From the Lower Saddle the trail follows Garnet Canyon out.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. Most parties then follow the Owen-Spalding approach toward the Upper Saddle and, before cresting it, turn left (west) to scramble the fairly easy ground to the Enclosure summit, where a worn trail may show. Early in the season the south couloir itself is an option, entered from the Dartmouth Basin side or from the Lower Saddle by staying left of the rib that divides it from the Exum gully.

review.notes: Route page for approach and reversal; trip report and Jim's Big Day page cross-check the descent via the Upper Saddle to the Lower Saddle.

set.descent_text: The technical climbing ends on a lengthy, exposed fourth-class ridge scramble to the Enclosure summit; many parties drop the rope there. Descend the easy ground toward the Upper Saddle, then follow the climbers trail to the Lower Saddle and out Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, just south of the Jenny Lake area, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand Teton and Middle Teton. The Valhalla Traverse is a system of ledges and slopes that leaves the Lower Saddle and circles the Enclosure. Follow just the opening stretch of the traverse, descend into the first big drainage, and then work up the scree to the southwest ridge. A large cairn marks the base of the route; scramble fourth-class slabs and third-class scree to reach it.

review.notes: Route page and trip report agree on the start and cairn; summit descent from the South Coulior and Jim's Big Day pages.
